value.title: Send to a role, the role queue and reply modes
Request store: migration 0034 role_requests
value.success: role_requests(id = the send's msg_id, project, role, instance, requester, body, in_reply_to, fyi, reply wake|fyi|none, limit_ms, state queued|delivered, holder, created_at, delivered_at) with a partial index on queued rows; SqliteOrchestration records a request, lists a role's queued requests oldest first (instance-less requests match any instance), lists every queued request, and marks one delivered. SCHEMA_VERSION 34.
value.notes: crates/store/migrations/0034_role_requests.sql, crates/store/src/role_requests.rs. Migration number claimed by pm-001.

value.title: Resolve a role send: one holder, several, mismatch, reply and limit
value.success: pij send role:<id>[/<instance>] (HTTP send and the shim, one shared function) resolves the project (--project or the caller's cwd), checks the role document exists in the governance worktree without launching anything, and finds live holders from open assignments plus the registry. One holder: an ordinary send (or FYI) to that seat through the cold-wake guard, recorded as a delivered request; the receipt carries request {id, role, instance, reply, limit_ms, state, holder}. Two or more: refuse listing them. A seat_roles disagreement for pm/pa/worker refuses with a named mismatch (C1). --reply wake|fyi|none (default wake) and --limit (default the role's default_limit, C5) are accepted only on role sends; role:x@machine and --command to a role refuse by name.
value.notes: crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs (+ http wiring in http/mod.rs and http/shim.rs), native CLI flags in crates/cli. Instance-less address on a many-holder role with several instance holders is several holders.

value.title: Queue and wake when no holder is live
value.success: With no live holder the request is queued (an --fyi send too, C2) and the project's PA holder, else the current prime designation, else a live prime-role seat, is woken once through the ordinary delivery path (cold wake audited, as the PA watchdog does) with the request and runnable next steps: revive the last holder (its context size) or assign a fresh seat. The PA digest lists queued requests until they drain (one store read per digest, no new timer). pij never starts a seat.
value.notes: Reuses pa_watchdog wake path; the digest section renders only when non-empty so existing digests are unchanged.

value.title: Drain the role queue on assign (C6)
value.success: An AfterAssign implementation, wired in build_services in place of NoHook, delivers the role's queued requests to the new holder in order (one delivery each, as the requester, FYIs held) and marks each delivered. A refused assign runs no hook and drains nothing.
value.notes: The hook is synchronous; it spawns the drain.

value.title: Cost readings
value.success: No new launch site, loop, poll or timer: spawn_sites.rs unchanged and green; the PR states per-verb cost; performance takes the live at-rest before and after.
value.notes: Role resolution reads the governance worktree in-process (root::find, a stat, one JSON read); no git launch.
